{{short description|Researcher}}

'''Renata Homem de Gouveia Xavier de Basto''' is a researcher in cell and [[developmental biology]]. She is currently a team leader at the [[Institut Curie]] in [[Paris]]. She is also the deputy director of the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] research Unit UMR144 'Cell biology and cancer'<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://science.institut-curie.org/research/multiscale-physics-biology-chemistry/umr144-subcellular-structure-and-cellular-dynamics/|title=Cell dynamics research: Institut Curie, subcellular structure and cellular dynamics|website=Centre de recherche de l'Institut Curie|language=en-US|access-date=2020-04-16}}</ref> at the Institut Curie which, comprises 14 research teams.

== Education and academic appointments ==
Renata Basto was born on December 17, 1972, in [[Mozambique]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.barrosbrito.com/7127.html|title=Renata Homem de Gouveia Xavier de BASTO|website=www.barrosbrito.com|access-date=2020-04-17}}</ref> She did her undergraduate studies in biology and genetics at the [[University of Lisbon]] in Portugal.<ref name="auto"/><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.insu.cnrs.fr/fr/personne/renata-basto|title=Renata Basto {{!}} INSU|website=www.insu.cnrs.fr|access-date=2020-04-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://arquivo.fct.pt/details?id=84209|title=Renata Homem de Gouveia Xavier de Basto|website=arquivo.fct.pt|language=en|access-date=2020-04-17}}</ref> She then did her PhD in the lab of Roger Karess in Paris. In 2002, she joined the laboratory of Jordan Raff in Cambridge (UK) to do her postdoctoral studies.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www2.bioch.ox.ac.uk/nanogroup/rafflab_alumni.html|title=Previous Lab Members {{!}} Raff Lab|website=www2.bioch.ox.ac.uk|access-date=2020-04-16}}</ref> In 2007, she was recruited at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] and started her own research team in 2008 at the [[Curie Institute (Paris)|Institut Curie]].<ref name=":1" /> In addition to running her own research group, she became the deputy director of the research Unit UMR144 'Cell biology and cancer'.<ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
During her PhD, Renata Basto studied the control of the transition from metaphase to anaphase in ''[[Drosophila melanogaster|Drosophila]]''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Basto|first1=Renata|last2=Gomes|first2=Rui|last3=Karess|first3=Roger E.|date=December 2000|title=Rough Deal and Zw10 are required for the metaphase checkpoint in Drosophila|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/ncb1200_939|journal=Nature Cell Biology|language=en|volume=2|issue=12|pages=939–943|doi=10.1038/35046592|pmid=11146659|s2cid=27007621|issn=1476-4679|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

During her postdoc in the lab of Jordan Raff, Renata Basto investigated the role of [[centriole]]s in flies during development. Her work led to two publications in the highly recognized journal [[Cell (journal)|''Cell'']], which have been cited more than 600 and 400 times respectively since publication.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Basto|first1=Renata|last2=Lau|first2=Joyce|last3=Vinogradova|first3=Tatiana|last4=Gardiol|first4=Alejandra|last5=Woods|first5=C. Geoffrey|last6=Khodjakov|first6=Alexey|last7=Raff|first7=Jordan W.|date=2006-06-30|title=Flies without Centrioles|journal=Cell|language=en|volume=125|issue=7|pages=1375–1386|doi=10.1016/j.cell.2006.05.025|pmid=16814722|s2cid=2080684|issn=0092-8674|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Basto|first1=Renata|last2=Brunk|first2=Kathrin|last3=Vinadogrova|first3=Tatiana|last4=Peel|first4=Nina|last5=Franz|first5=Anna|last6=Khodjakov|first6=Alexey|last7=Raff|first7=Jordan W.|date=2008-06-13|title=Centrosome Amplification Can Initiate Tumorigenesis in Flies|url= |journal=Cell|language=en|volume=133|issue=6|pages=1032–1042|doi=10.1016/j.cell.2008.05.039|pmid=18555779|issn=0092-8674|pmc=2653712}}</ref>

She is considered a reference in the field of centrosomes biology and has edited a book about methods to study cilia and flagella.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5-CoBAAAQBAJ&q=%22renata+basto%22+cilia+book&pg=PP1|title=Methods in Cilia and Flagella|date=2015-03-26|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=978-0-12-802640-3|language=en}}</ref> She is the author of 58 publications and has been cited 1,929 times.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.semanticscholar.org/author/Renata-Basto/6610809|title=Renata Basto {{!}} Semantic Scholar|website=www.semanticscholar.org|language=en-US|access-date=2020-04-17}}</ref>
